issues.legal_issue: Mutation of land in revenue records does not create or extinguish title to the land and has no presumptive value as to title.
material_facts: The dispute concerned entries in revenue records relating to land.
Civil suits concerning the land were pending between the parties.
issues.conclusion: Mutation in revenue records does not create or extinguish title and has no presumptive value as to title; it only enables the person in whose favour it is ordered to pay the land revenue.
issues.legal_principle: As held in Sawarni (Smt.) v. Inder Kaur, (1996) 6 SCC 223; Balwant Singh v. Daulat Singh, (1997) 7 SCC 137; and Narasamma v. State of Karnataka, (2009) 5 SCC 591, mutation entries do not determine ownership and serve only the purpose of enabling payment of land revenue.

predicates.land_revenue_entry_made: An authority made an entry in the revenue records concerning land.
predicates.mutation_entry_does_not_create_or_exting: A revenue-record mutation does not create or extinguish title to the land.

issues.definition: When an authority makes a revenue-record entry concerning land, the entry does not create or extinguish title to that land.

issues.legal_issue: A court hearing an appeal concerning revenue-record entries should not undertake factual inquiries into the correctness or origin of those entries when related civil suits are pending and the entries do not determine title.
material_facts: The appeal arose from a dispute about entries in revenue records relating to land.
Civil suits concerning the same land were pending between the parties.
The factual dispute included whether the entries were properly made and at whose instance they were made.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to inquire into the factual correctness or origin of the entries in the appeal because related civil suits were pending and the entries neither decided nor extinguished the parties’ title.
issues.legal_principle: Revenue entries do not determine or extinguish title, as explained in Sawarni (Smt.) v. Inder Kaur, (1996) 6 SCC 223; Balwant Singh v. Daulat Singh, (1997) 7 SCC 137; and Narasamma v. State of Karnataka, (2009) 5 SCC 591. In the circumstances, factual inquiries into the entries were not proper in the appeal while civil suits concerning the land remained pending.

predicates.appeal_concerning_revenue_entries: A party brought an appeal concerning entries made in land revenue records.
predicates.related_civil_suits_pending: The parties had civil suits pending concerning the same land.
predicates.entry_correctness_or_origin_disputed: A party disputed whether the revenue entries were properly made or who caused them to be made.
predicates.appellate_court_declines_factual_inquiry: The appellate court does not investigate the factual correctness or origin of the revenue entries.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns revenue entries, related civil suits remain pending, and the correctness or origin of the entries is disputed, the appellate court declines to investigate those facts.
